source.title: Neighborhood-Aware Neural Architecture Search
source.authors: Xiao-Fang Wang; Sheng-Cao Cao; Mengtian Li; Kris M. Kitani

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether architecture-space neighborhood flatness tracks test error using a different flatness measure from the weight-space measure in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study measures architecture-neighborhood variance and compares average validation and test errors for flat- and sharp-neighborhood architecture groups. It does not test the listed training recipes, width scaling, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, magnitude-aware weight perturbations, or memorized-example removal.
record.test_reason: The study tests architecture-space neighborhood flatness against test error, a related but different construct from V7's magnitude-scaled weight perturbations and training–test gaps. It tests none of V1–V8. Its architecture-space results do not qualify as T2 evidence for V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that flat-minimum architectures generalize better and that aggregating neighborhood performance improves architecture selection. This concerns architecture-space perturbations and search-to-evaluation generalization, not magnitude-aware weight sharpness or training–test gaps.
record.recipe_differences: Measures architecture-space neighborhood variance and tests NAS architecture selection; it does not perturb trained network weights or measure a training-test gap.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported flat-versus-sharp comparison is repeated using CIFAR-10 validation error at epochs 30, 60, 90 and 120; the stated pattern holds across those epoch choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Among the 100 architectures with lowest CIFAR-10 search-time validation error, the 50 with lower neighborhood variance have lower average test error on all three datasets. At epoch 90, errors are 6.23 versus 6.66, 28.90 versus 30.00, and 55.17 versus 56.41 percent. The direction persists at epochs 30, 60, and 120.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within selected low-validation-error NAS-Bench-201 architectures, lower architecture-neighborhood variance is associated with lower final test error and better transfer across datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Table C shows that max aggregation selects architectures with lower neighborhood variance than the baseline, 1.83 versus 5.58, but higher test error on all three datasets. Section B.4 attributes this to failing to preserve good performance at the reference architecture.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low architecture-neighborhood variance alone does not guarantee low test error; reference-architecture performance also matters.

record.problems: The flat-versus-sharp comparison uses groups selected from the 100 architectures with lowest CIFAR-10 validation error and reports group averages without uncertainty estimates. The test datasets differ from the CIFAR-10 search dataset, so this does not measure a same-distribution training-test gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to interpolate.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout effects and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbation tolerance, its association with training–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The record's blanket statement that test datasets differ from the search dataset is incorrect: CIFAR-10 is used for both search and evaluation; CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-16-120 assess transfer of the architecture, evaluated on each dataset. Group averages lack uncertainty estimates. The Table C qualification concerns a separate architecture-space claim, so it warrants no verdict or missing-row entry for V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Memorizing random labels and generalizing on natural labels under the same training recipes.
Widening one-hidden-layer ReLU networks beyond the interpolation threshold.
Comparisons of convolutional and fully connected networks and the effects of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers and tuning or recipe changes.
Large- versus small-batch training under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout and its interaction with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Weight-magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, training-test gap ranking, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
